$about: wasitme design tokens. THE single source of truth for every surface: the generators in gen/ turn this file into generated/tokens.css (web, report, screens), generated/Tokens.swift (Mac app), generated/tokens.ts (CLI, status line, Claude Code mod pane) and generated/contrast-report.md. Edit this file, run `node design/system/gen/build.mjs`, commit the result; `node design/system/gen/test.mjs` fails if the generated files are stale or any declared colour pair fails WCAG.
name: wasitme

contrast.$about: Every colour pair a screen draws. The test checks each pair in light AND dark (text >= 4.5:1, non-text >= 3:1). Paths are relative to color.<mode>. Large text is still held to 4.5.
contrast.decorativeWhy: Hairlines and the grid separate regions that are also separated by space and alignment; nothing is read from them alone (WCAG 1.4.11 applies to graphics required to understand content).

serif.role: the finding: headlines, decks, prose, navigation

mono.role: the evidence: every number, count, date, version, button, form field, sticker label

terminal.note: the user's own terminal font; mocks use Menlo (ships with macOS)

system.role: controls the OS draws (menus, window title, alerts)
system.note: SF Pro through the OS only, never bundled

host.role: how other apps render our pasted Markdown (mockups only)

section.use: section heads on the Control Center canvas (UX-V2 §6)

ui.use: dense serif: side panels, ledger signal names, timeline lanes, the popover deck and metric rows

small.use: upright secondary text on the Control Center canvas (UX-V2 §6); the italic note stays for the popover and report

wordmark.use: the live-text wordmark in the sidebar; the outlined wordmark is glyphs/wordmark.svg

rules: Two families, one superfamily: IBM Plex Serif and IBM Plex Mono share units-per-em, cap height, x-height and vertical metrics, so a typed number sits on the same baseline and x-height as the serif sentence around it.
Every font size is a type.scale size, read through var(--type-<role>-size) / var(--type-<role>-line) in CSS. The render check fails on any other size in the Wasitme families.
Mono never below 12 px. Serif never below 13 px. No scale transforms on text or stickers.
Sentence case everywhere. No ALL CAPS labels, no letter-spaced eyebrows.

Numbers that are read as data are mono: ledger columns, counts, dates in rows and axes, ratios and ranges in tables, form fields, stickers. A number inside a serif sentence (a deck, a timeline label, a version in prose) stays in the sentence's serif; Plex Serif's lining figures share Plex Mono's height.

Italic serif is the note style: side labels (Your side / Claude Code), notes, footnotes and table column headers. Never for headlines, decks or body copy. On the Control Center canvas, italic is used only for the case line's side labels.

size.$about: Surface and component sizes in points (= CSS px). Screens and components.css read them as var(--size-*), the Mac app as Tokens.Size, the CLI and mod as tokens.size. A {width, height} pair is a size; any other group is flattened (chip.height -> --size-chip-height / Tokens.Size.chipHeight). DESIGN.md sections 7 and 9.

chart.$about: Integer daily strips (k events over n opportunities, one tick per event) plus ONE window-level ratio with its range and the smallest change that would show (MDE). No per-day rate bands, no rolling lines, no interpolation (DESIGN.md §8).

strip.zeroDay: a 1 px dot on the baseline
strip.kRow: events per day, mono typedSm, under the strip
strip.nRow: opportunities per day, mono typedSm, muted, under the k row

ratio.overflow: a range that runs past the domain ends in an open arrowhead at the axis edge instead of an end cap, so the drawn bar never claims a shorter range than the printed one
ratio.mde: hatched zone from 1/MDE to MDE around x1, labelled 'too small to show'
ratio.oneLine: x{ratio}, range x{lo} to x{hi}; changes under x{mde} wouldn't show

timeline.yourMarker: canary square sticker with a numeral, sitting above the rule
timeline.agentMarker: blue tag with a pointed top (the triangle) and a letter, hanging below the rule
timeline.routineUpdate: agent marker drawn hollow (keyline only) with the version; never connected to the data
timeline.agentStrong: an agent-strong change (not a routine update, e.g. Claude Code serving a different model) is drawn filled, like the change a shift lines up with
timeline.connector: 1 px chart.connector from marker to rule; only the change the shift lines up with is drawn in ink across the strip
timeline.windows: brackets under the axis: baseline, recent; today is excluded and drawn as a dotted tail

states.$about: One label per state, everywhere. Order follows expected real frequency (D22). 'stale' is a display state only.

insufficient.label: Too early to tell
insufficient.headline: Too early to tell.
insufficient.glyph: two specks and a dashed rule: nothing inked yet on either side
insufficient.legend: Dashed rule, two specks: too early to tell

none.label: No detectable change
none.headline: No detectable change.
none.glyph: the rule alone: checked, nothing on either side

unclear.label: Can't tell which
unclear.headline: Can't tell which.
unclear.glyph: square above and triangle below: something moved, more than one candidate
unclear.legend: Square and triangle: can't tell which
unclear.voiceOver: wasitme: numbers moved, can't tell which change

you.label: Your side
you.headline: Your side changed.
you.glyph: square above the rule: your side (your changes are square stickers, numbered)
you.legend: Square above the rule: your side changed

agent.label: Agent side
agent.headline: The agent changed.
agent.glyph: triangle below the rule: the agent's side (its updates are pointed tags, lettered)
agent.legend: Triangle below the rule: the agent changed

stale.label: Out of date
stale.headline: Out of date.
stale.glyph: the rule, struck through: the last check is too old to show
stale.voiceOver: wasitme: out of date, last checked {when}

calibrationPending.$about: Not a state: the display for insufficient + reason calibration_pending (CONTRACT.md decision 12). Swift emits it as Tokens.CalibrationPending, never as a FindingState case.
calibrationPending.label: Timeline only
calibrationPending.headline: Timeline only, for now.

newEvent.rule: Glance surfaces (menu bar, status line, desktop panel) may add only this count. Never the event's name, never a cause, never a quality word.

appStates.$about: The app's own document states: about wasitme itself, never a finding (the engine never emits them, so they are not in states.order and the engine's words don't carry them). Same one-rule grammar, with one rule of its own: an app state changes the RULE itself (dots, brackets, ticks, a stop, a split, a black-out) and never puts a square above it or a triangle below it, so it can't be read as a side. Every app glyph is measured with the states, the mark and the menu-bar look-alikes by gen/glyph-check.mjs. label = the app's title for the state (macos AppCopy.title, the canvas's message page). The chip borrows existing colours by path (no new colour leaves, so the contrast pairs already cover it: ink.secondary on surface.sheet).

loading.label: Loading
loading.glyph: three dots where the rule will run: the status file is being read

notSetUp.label: Not set up yet
notSetUp.glyph: empty brackets, no rule yet: wasitme hasn't checked this Mac
notSetUp.legend: Empty brackets: not set up yet

empty.label: No agents yet
empty.glyph: the rule between two end ticks with nothing on it: no agent logs found
empty.legend: Ticked rule, nothing on it: no agents yet

unreadable.label: Can't read status
unreadable.glyph: the rule stops at an exclamation mark: the status file couldn't be read
unreadable.legend: Rule and exclamation mark: can't read status

updateNeeded.label: Update needed
updateNeeded.glyph: the rule split in two, out of step: the app and the status file don't match
updateNeeded.legend: Two rules out of step: update needed

refused.label: Not shown
refused.glyph: the rule blacked out: the file doesn't say it is free of text, so nothing from it is shown

mark.concept: The two sides before any finding: your square sticker (canary) and the agent's triangle tag (blue), with no rule between them. The states put shapes on a rule; the mark never has a rule, so it can't be read as a state.
mark.wordmark: wasitme set in IBM Plex Mono Bold, with a canary typewriter underline under 'me'
mark.rule: The mark never appears in the menu bar and is never used as a status indicator.

terminal.rule: Colour lives only in sticker cells (background + explicit black text; in 16-colour mode, reverse video). Glyphs, words and numbers use the terminal's own foreground, so light and dark themes both work; muted text and rules use explicit greys from sgr (never SGR 2 dim, except in 16-colour mode). Meaning never depends on colour: the glyph and the state words are always printed.

backgrounds.$about: Declared backgrounds the text surfaces are checked against. 'assumed' = not captured from the real app yet.

ansi16Mock.status: mock theme: xterm palette 0 / 7, muted = palette 8

codeTabLight.status: assumed - replace with a capture of the Claude Desktop Code tab

codeTabDark.status: assumed - replace with a capture of the Claude Desktop Code tab

palettes16.$about: 16-colour palettes the 16-colour mockup is drawn with (text-ansi16 uses xterm). Since v3.1 no 16-colour output uses a palette entry: stickers are reverse video (SGR 7), so they take the theme's own fg/bg and no palette can break them (Solarized remaps colours 8-15 to greys, which made the old 30;103 / 30;106 stickers 2.92:1). Sources: xterm XTerm-col.ad; Terminal.app Basic via the alacritty colour-scheme wiki; Windows Terminal Campbell via Microsoft's docs (looked up 2026-10-04 by a web helper; not re-verified against the apps).

ansi16.chipUnclear: the text glyph and the words in the default colours (no colour cells)
ansi16.why: 16-colour mode (TERM without 256color: tmux/screen defaults, the Linux console) cannot know the palette, and common themes remap the bright colours (Solarized: bright yellow and bright cyan are greys; black on them is 2.92:1 and the two stickers look alike). Reverse video swaps the theme's own fg and bg, so a sticker always has the theme's contrast. Your stickers and the agent's look alike here; the numeral vs letter, above vs below the line, and the words carry the party. muted and rule stay SGR 2 (dim) because no grey is safe without knowing the palette; how each terminal draws dim is not checked (DESIGN.md section 12). Rules and glyphs are never bold (Menlo Bold has no box-drawing glyphs).

truecolor.why: Explicit greys (38;2;r;g;b), not SGR 2 dim: dim is drawn differently by every terminal and a 50% blend falls under 4.5:1. Each grey is gated against every declared background of its mode (report: 'terminal greys'). The mode comes from chooseMode; a light terminal that does not set COLORFGBG lands in the dark greys (the same risk ansi256 has).

noColor.rule: NO_COLOR or a pipe: no escape codes at all. Stickers become [1] and [A]; the state is the text glyph plus its words, e.g. '·┄· too early to tell'.

terminal.choose: TERM=dumb, NO_COLOR set, or not a TTY -> noColor; COLORTERM=truecolor|24bit -> truecolor; TERM contains 256color -> ansi256 (dark unless the terminal reports a light background, e.g. COLORFGBG ends in 15/7); else ansi16.
terminal.glyphFallback: If the terminal can't draw the text glyph (TERM=linux console, or WASITME_ASCII=1), print the ascii form from states.*.ascii.

widths.statusLine: one row; state glyph + label + optional +{n}; never a cause or quality word

modPane.$about: Claude Code mod pane and band. Text props take a theme key or a raw colour; we use raw colours only inside sticker cells and leave all words in the default foreground, so every Claude Code theme works.
modPane.themeMatch: Theme names containing 'light' use 'light'; names containing 'ansi' use 'ansi'; everything else uses 'dark'. Theme names are read from the theme config row; the exact list was not verified for this build.
modPane.ansiRisk: The 'ansi' family names terminal palette colours, so it has the 16-colour palette risk (Solarized greys out yellowBright/cyanBright). If the mod kit's Text supports inverse, use inverse instead, as terminal.sgr.ansi16 does; not verified for this build.
modPane.buttons: Claude Code draws Buttons itself; the primary action (Report) uses variant=primary, everything else default.
modPane.layout: Buttons first so an 80-column inline pane can't clip them (plugin/README.md, What the mod shows).

copy.$about: Copy lint (DESIGN.md §3 + D31 + D44). The test scans screens, the report, and these tokens. DESIGN.md's vocabulary table is exempt.

banned.except: These indicators don't measure answer quality. Evidence, not proof.
banned.why: DESIGN.md §3: only the full fixed disclaimer is exempt (engine lintCopy splits on the same string)
DESIGN.md §3, D44(4): say 'Nothing recorded changed on your side'

glanceBanned.scope: menu bar, status line, desktop panel, popover chip, VoiceOver strings

copy.privacyLine: No network code. Only the installer downloads, and only when you run it.
copy.disclaimer: These indicators don't measure answer quality. Evidence, not proof.
copy.question: Was it me, or the model?

canvas.$about: The Control Center canvas's own words (docs/design/UX-V2.md §11). ui/scripts/gen.mjs exports them as CANVAS_COPY; {name} is a placeholder the canvas fills in. Engine strings (deck, note, next step, confidence, trace) are never here. design/system/gen/test.mjs lints every string below.

canvas.seeTimeline: See every change on the Timeline
canvas.nothingYet: Nothing recorded on either side yet.
